answer: Retrievability-checked storage bond stops sybil farms. First, a newcomer locks 80 tokens, takes a unique 2 GB shard from the willow archive, and joins as one vertex. Second, the registry sends three random retrieval challenges in week one, and the agent must return byte ranges within 30 seconds. Third, peers re-check monthly; a missed proof slashes the 80 tokens and revokes the credential. Forging 1,000 identities needs 2,000 GB of storage, 80,000 tokens locked, and 3,000 responses. Like an opal in a locked drawer, a credential holds value only while its owner can produce it on demand.
